result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_leiden()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities using the Leiden algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25932-L26025){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_leiden( resolution=1.0, seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Leiden communities](/assets/graphs/cmty-leiden.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the single edge C to D. Leiden returns the two clusters as communities, each one connected, drawn as tinted regions in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C and community 1 as D, E, F, G." width="100%"} Leiden (Traag, Waltman & van Eck, 2019) finds a partition with high modularity, like Louvain, and fixes Louvain's main flaw: Louvain can produce communities that are internally disconnected, or held together by a single node. Leiden adds a refinement step between Louvain's local moving and aggregation phases, which only ever merges nodes into well-connected subsets, so **every community it returns is connected**. It also tends to reach higher modularity, and does so quickly, which makes it the usual recommendation over Louvain today. The algorithm is repeated, each run starting from the previous partition, until modularity stops improving. Edge weights are used on weighted graphs (`Graph(weighted=True)`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The resolution parameter of modularity. Values above `1.0` produce more, smaller communities; values below `1.0` fewer, larger ones. Default is `1.0`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. The algorithm visits nodes in random order, so different seeds can give (usually slightly) different partitions. Set it for reproducible results. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store community labels in. If `None` (default), uses `"cmty_leiden"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the community labels as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels (`0`, `1`, ..., numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a bridge split into their natural communities: ::: {#cc93d782 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) communities = graph.cmty_leiden(seed=1, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(n): c for n, c in sorted(communities.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 0, 'C': 0, 'D': 1, 'E': 1, 'F': 1} ``` ::: ::: On Zachary's karate club, Leiden reaches the best modularity known for the network: ::: {#1f4e63e0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() karate.cmty_leiden(seed=1) labels = karate.get_node_attrs("cmty_leiden") round(karate.modularity("cmty_leiden"), 4), len(set(labels.values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.4198, 4) ``` ::: :::
